# Review #354: docs must match the command users actually run

Exact head `d5813cada7341fbda7f2816c3d6679f48800db4f`; baseline/main `387362db777476a26a789f9e5e15b356e046cc6b`. Read-only detached worktree; all probes in one private archive.

Verdict: **block**, commit `1b97a6b50178223fbbbe324dc26fedc75cc302a7`, `reviewer/outputs/2026-11/25-verdict-pr-354-d5813ca.dd.json`. B354-R1-01 through -03 are false default-output, history-scope and no-start command claims. B354-R1-04 is a nonblocking upstream step-state note. The role request was answered by the verdict writer.

## Carry forward

- A daemon JSON response is not proof of the ordinary CLI view. The pod renderer drops pod state, member harness/model, owner holders, deliverable stages and log, and session transcript paths. A local synthetic HTTP envelope through the actual CLI reproduced these omissions; JSON retained the fields. Document `--json` where that view is intended, rather than widening a docs-only fix into a rendering feature.
- `pij sessions --history` without `--seat` folds only non-tombstoned roster entries. A closed seat remains readable by explicit `--seat`; pod history explicitly names members.
- `pij spawn` is still an unported shim route. Manual joining after pod `--no-start` uses `pij-rs spawn --as role:<id>[/<instance>] --pod <pod>`, with the role's harness when omitted.
- Pod `set` and deliverable write-back use a one-directional safety brake: removing it sends more, never changes the decision policy. Write-back is skipped if any live destination holder is a degraded member of this pod. Ordinary sends stay untouched.
- One canary task waits on events to a single 15-minute deadline; it is not a poll, but does have a bounded timer. A later member confirmation recomputes and persists its degraded outcome.
- The template is named by path, never searched. Down uses one git status read, then the existing close-stop handler; keep-open members are spared and consulted roles untouched. Context history seeks and caps at 256 KiB, with `unknown` for unavailable usage.
- A newly complete step can still depend on an upstream row marked in-progress. Reconcile states using delivery receipts; do not assume a merged implementation changed its workstream row.
- C34 was amended to **one reviewer, one round**. The author fixes and the prime range-diffs. Earlier two-round GitHub memories are outdated; their correction tools were unavailable in this seat.

## Proof discipline

Use `git archive <full-head>` into a recorded private folder. Shared-build touches crate-root mtimes, so do not build in the read-only review checkout. **Never export `GIT_*` into a test runner.** Fixture children inherit them: `git init`, config, commits and worktree operations then target the shared repository, not the fixture's cwd. Read-only intentions do not constrain subprocess writes. Use CI for Git-dependent archive tests, or an approved private repository with its own metadata. Archive builds may be version-unstamped; compiled source equality is a separate proof. Keep the shared target, lock, niceness 19, four-job cap, incremental disabled and 25 GiB floor. Copy out the built binary while holding the lock before another worktree can replace it.

The private docs build passed 12 CLI docs tests. The copied binary printed the page byte-for-byte with no reachable daemon; docs-bundle-check matched all 15 pages. Exact-head CI had both Node matrix jobs and Rust jobs green, and both Node jobs ran the real bundle checker. No dependencies were installed or symlinked (C25).

The attempted full local gate is **invalid proof**. Exported `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` reached fixture tests and changed shared core.worktree and synthetic user attribution, created one fixture ref and five empty review-HEAD commits. I stopped, notified the PM and prime, and waited for coordinated repair. The prime removed the shared config/ref and pruned worktrees; I cleared the Git environment, CAS-restored only the detached review HEAD, verified the exact head and clean source, and deleted the exact archive after approval. Main's head stayed unchanged. The broad gate is not counted; only focused pre-incident checks and exact-head CI are relied on.

The deployed verdict writer is `pij output verdict --role reviewer --subject pr:354 --head <full-head> --result block --answers <request-id>`. `pij verdict` is unported. The writer persists the verdict and answers its role request; never write governance output files manually.

## Harness retrospective

magicWand: one focused doc-to-ordinary-CLI fixture proving documented fields and example commands, including JSON-only qualifications, unported shim verbs and closed-seat history.

difficulties:
- degrading / proof gap: the bundle checker proves source equality, not prose truth or the default rendered view. A green bundle and unit suite missed three normal-use documentation inaccuracies.
- annoying / workflow: no review procedure exists among the listed procedures; private archive setup and exact-head provenance are still re-derived.
- degrading / tooling: dependency-free review archives cannot supply TypeScript gates. Do not symlink node_modules; distinguish reviewer proof, CI proof and unavailable sensors.
- degrading / isolation incident: inherited Git location variables redirected fixture writes into shared metadata. A review launcher should reject `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` before any test runner; until such a guard is approved, never export them.

The fixture/recipe is a proposal under C35, not authorization for new work. This role note preserves the lesson without changing the reviewed worktree or another writer's ledgers.
